results.title: Explains part 2 in plain words for a non-physicist
results.idealItem: Presenter (explains a part) + Knowing when to talk
results.chapter: Meeting 3: Understanding the results and observations (parts 2 and 3)
results.asked: Suppose someone joins who hasn't done physics since school. How would you explain what this part says, in plain words?
results.answer: , fifteen meters per second at thirty degrees, the range here works out to about twenty-one meters, and with a two-meter ledge, about twenty-three. I’d say, we’re just describing a thrown ball in two separate pieces. Sideways, it just keeps coasting. Vertically, gravity slows it going up, stops it at the top, then pulls it down faster and faster. That combination makes a smooth arc. From that you can work out, how long it’s in the air, how high it gets, and how far it lands. The numbers in these formulas just spell that out. And they note things like, forty-five degrees gives the longest range, steeper angles stay up longer, and straight up means no horizontal distance.
results.why: It omits the fourfold speed-scaling and mass-independence points, never clearly states sideways speed times airtime, and introduces an unsupported ledge example with an inaccurate range.
